Treatment
Th ere is no cure for SLE and the mainstay of treatment is the 
pharmacologic management of acute, periodic ﬂ are-ups and
management of the less severe, chronic forms of the disease. 
Drugs used to treat the musculoskeletal manifestations of SLE 
range from over-the-counter nonsteroidal anti-inﬂ ammatory 
drugs (e.g., such as aspirin, ibuprofen, and naproxen) and anti-
malarial drugs (e.g., hydroxychloroquine) during the chronic 
periods of remission to relatively high-dose corticosteroids 
during instances of severe ﬂ are-ups.47, 66
